name: Phil Spector
hook: A producer who treated the pop single as a wall of sound built from dozens of musicians, whose method Brian Wilson built Pet Sounds on, and who was convicted of murder in 2009.

blurb.age13: Phil Spector was born in the Bronx in 1939. In the early 1960s he ran his own label, Philles, and made hit singles like the Ronettes' 'Be My Baby' (1963) by filling a Hollywood studio with musicians all playing at once, then drowning it in echo. People called it the Wall of Sound. Brian Wilson of the Beach Boys built his records on it. Spector later produced the Beatles' 'Let It Be' and the Ramones. In 2009 he was convicted of murdering the actress Lana Clarkson, and he died in prison in 2021.
blurb.adult: Born in the Bronx in 1939. He co-founded Philles Records with Lester Sill in late 1961 and made his Wall of Sound at Gold Star Studios in Hollywood with the session players later called the Wrecking Crew: several guitars, pianos and percussionists doubling the same parts, recorded through heavy reverb and echo, mixed for mono and AM radio. The Ronettes' 'Be My Baby' (1963) reached number two. He was brought in to finish the Beatles' abandoned 'Let It Be' sessions (1970), adding orchestral overdubs McCartney objected to, and produced the Ramones' 'End of the Century' (1980). In 2009 he was convicted of the second-degree murder of Lana Clarkson, killed at his house on 3 February 2003, and sentenced to 19 years to life. He died in prison custody in 2021. His conduct in the studio, including accounts of guns at sessions, is disputed in detail by the musicians who were there, and is stated on the edges where it is sourced.
